findings.source_passage: its very blinding palpableness must have been the cause
findings.why_it_matters: This clause is Melville's characteristic ironic paradox — the compasses' error went unnoticed precisely because it was so blindingly obvious — and its omission removes a key moment of narrative wit.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full sentence: 'Upon this every soul was confounded; for the phenomenon just then observed by Ahab had unaccountably escaped every one else; but its very blinding palpableness must have been the cause.'

findings.source_passage: the before magnetic steel was of no more use than an old wife's knitting needle
findings.source_locator: explanatory paragraph on magnetic accidents, mid-segment
findings.why_it_matters: This simile is tonally and rhetorically distinctive — the homely 'old wife's knitting needle' against the charged masculine world of the ship — and encapsulates Melville's habitual bathetic deflation; its loss flattens the explanatory digression.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full closing sentence of the magnetic-accident paragraph, including the knitting-needle simile and the detail about the kelson.

findings.source_passage: Accessory, perhaps, to the impulse dictating the thing he was now about to do, were certain prudential motives, whose object might have been to revive the spirits of his crew by a stroke of his subtile skill
findings.source_locator: paragraph before Ahab's speech to the crew beginning 'Men, said he'
findings.why_it_matters: This paragraph of authorial speculation on Ahab's motives — prudential calculation beneath mystic performance — is a critical interpretive node about whether Ahab's theatrics are cynically instrumental or genuinely felt; its complete omission removes a layer of psychological ambiguity.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full 'Accessory, perhaps' paragraph before the crew-address speech, as it carries interpretive weight about Ahab's leadership psychology.

findings.source_passage: Deliberately standing before the binnacle, and eyeing the transpointed compasses, the old man, with the sharp of his extended hand, now took the precise bearing of the sun
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Deliberately standing before the binnacle'
findings.why_it_matters: The detail of taking the sun's bearing 'with the sharp of his extended hand' is a vivid, physically specific gesture that characterises Ahab's bodily authority; the draft collapses this to 'satisfied they were exactly inverted' and loses the visual precision.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the hand-as-instrument detail: 'with the sharp of his extended hand, now took the precise bearing of the sun.'

summary: Three medium-severity losses — the 'blinding palpableness' irony, the 'old wife's knitting needle' simile, and the entire 'Accessory, perhaps' paragraph on Ahab's prudential motives — collectively flatten Melville's ironic voice and remove a key interpretive node about Ahab's psychology, triggering regeneration.
